Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The HighRequestErrorRate alert for frontend is firing because the frontend's gRPC calls to the ad service are refused at the network layer. The alerting rule for group opentelemetrydemo.frontend.goldensignal is sum by (service_name, namespace)(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0, and at 19:47:57 it reported frontend 4.4555 and frontend-proxy 1.9222 error spans/s (alert activeAt 19:44:57, state firing). Sampled error spans show the frontend's failures concentrated on oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (0.722/s ERROR) and the /api/data route, while the ad service itself records no ERROR spans. The frontend container logs the exact error '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.53.164:8080' on its getAds client call, i.e. the ad Service ClusterIP 10.96.53.164 port 8080; the earliest such line in the sampled window is 19:44:28Z. The ad Service object is the only otel-demo Service carrying a second writer: besides the Helm apply at 19:36:00Z its managedFieldsSummary shows manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' Update at 19:43:27Z, and its current spec maps port 8080 to targetPort 8089 and port 9465 to targetPort 9474, while the ad container declares containerPort 8080/9465 and runs with AD_PORT=8080 and no readiness probe. Endpoints for ad resolve to pod ad-6478f46d8-wxx8r port 8089/9474, so callers are sent to a port the ad container is not configured to serve. Traffic to ad (server spans and its GET /metrics scrape spans) falls to zero shortly after 19:43:27, and the ad pod itself is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, so the refusal is a Service routing fault rather than an ad application crash. No NetworkPolicy exists in otel-demo, and every flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap (including adFailure) has defaultVariant off, so neither of those candidate causes is supported. The same error signal is carried to frontend-proxy and load-generator, whose own error spans are visible.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so it is unknown who or what 'OpenAPI-Generator' is and what exact patch it sent to Service ad at 19:43:27Z; managedFieldsSummary records only the writer and time, not the changed fields.

The Service spec as it stood before 19:43:27Z cannot be read (no resourceVersion history), so the earlier targetPort values (presumably 8080/9465) are inferred from the fact that ad served requests until then, not directly observed.

The ad container's live listening sockets could not be inspected; AD_PORT=8080, containerPort 8080 and the absence of any readiness probe are configuration facts, not a socket-level confirmation, so the exact reason port 8089 refuses remains inferred.

Only otel-demo Services and Deployments were examined for post-19:36 writes; whether the same writer touched objects in other namespaces is unchecked. A query for otel-demo Deployments written after 19:36:30Z returned nothing (no_data), so nothing is concluded from it.
The ad container's log stream ends at 19:43:25.579968Z while its server spans continue until roughly 19:45, and the cause of that gap in log coverage is unknown.

The recommendation service's low-rate flagd.evaluation.v2.Service/EventStream error (0.00339/s at 19:48:04Z) and its earlier get_product_list/ListProducts errors are not attributed to this cause; their origin was not established, and its pending alert is a separate signal.
The precise second when traffic began failing relative to the 19:43:27Z Service write cannot be resolved because the sampled span rates alternate on scrape alignment (roughly one-minute granularity).
No trace-level parent references were used to prove the frontend->frontend-proxy->load-generator chain; those spans are attributed only to their own service identities.
next_steps: Diff Service ad against the deployed Helm chart values to confirm the expected targetPorts and re-apply the chart so the Service matches the ad container's 8080/9465 ports.
Use cluster audit logs or the controllers' credentials to identify the client behind field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' and the exact request it issued at 2026-11-25T19:43:27Z.

Have a human verify from inside the cluster that pod ad-6478f46d8-wxx8r listens on 8080 and not on 8089, and add a readiness probe on the ad container so a broken service port is distinguishable from an unhealthy pod.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
